meta.triageRationale: One cohesive change in the daemon's MCP registration (src/daemon/mcp-register.ts): when the vibe client is registered, ensure the user-level ~/.vibe/AGENTS.md carries the insrc steering block between insrc:steering markers, replacing any existing marked block so re-registration and future releases update it in place instead of duplicating. Clear approach, a handful of files plus tests; no design ceremony beyond that.

findings.premise: The four acceptance criteria (ac1 replace-on-reregistration-no-duplicate, ac2 asset-change-updates-content, ac3 surrounding-content-byte-identical, ac4 idempotent-second-call-writes-nothing) each map to a real, passing unit test in src/daemon/__tests__/mcp-register.test.ts, and no out-of-scope capability (e.g. project-level AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md writing, versioning tokens) was added.
findings.evidence: mcp-register.test.ts contains 'creates AGENTS.md ... idempotent on second call' (ac4), 'replaces only the marked span on re-registration (future release updates content in place), preserves surrounding user content' (ac1/ac2/ac3), and 'malformed markers ... guarded no-op' — these exercise create/replace/idempotent/preserve exactly as the LLD's acceptance-mapping table (section 6) states; no project-level write or version-token logic was added anywhere in mcp-register.ts.

findings.premise: Before this Story, nothing wrote the user-level ~/.vibe/AGENTS.md, and vibe has no `mcp list` (pre-checked via config.toml instead), as the HLD-context paragraph states.
findings.evidence: clientPlans() in src/daemon/mcp-register.ts gives vibe no `listArgs` (only claude/codex have one), confirming the no-`mcp list` claim; a repo-wide grep for 'AGENTS.md' shows every other reference (steering-inject.ts, ReposPane.tsx, command.ts, repo.ts) is about the project-level repo AGENTS.md, not ~/.vibe/AGENTS.md — upsertVibeAgentsSteering (this Story's new function) is the only code that reads/writes the user-level file.

findings.premise: Section 2.2 names `vibeAgentsSteeringBlock: () => string` as a contract function of this Story, reading the shipped `prompts/steering-block.md` asset.
findings.evidence: No such function exists anywhere in the source tree (grep for `vibeAgentsSteeringBlock` only matches the LLD.md and its JSON artifact, never a `.ts` file). The actual implementation has no new asset-reading function at all: `upsertVibeAgentsSteering` in src/daemon/mcp-register.ts:201-213 uses `const block = deps.steeringBlockText ?? readSteeringBlock;` — it reuses the existing `readSteeringBlock` from steering-inject.ts directly through an optional seam, exactly as section 3.1 separately (and correctly) describes. Section 2.2 documents a contract member that was never built and that contradicts the Story's own 'reused, not new' framing in section 3.1. [files: src/daemon/mcp-register.ts, docs/standalone/write-versioned-marker-delimited-insrc-steering-E20261101866873ca/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Drop section 2.2 (or rename it to document the `steeringBlockText` seam + its `readSteeringBlock` default) so the contract table matches what was actually built.

findings.premise: Section 4's shared-contract row states 'registerMcpClients calls upsertVibeAgentsSteering on the vibe path after the MCP outcome'.
findings.evidence: In `registerOne` (src/daemon/mcp-register.ts:324-397), the vibe steering upsert block (lines 340-347) runs immediately after the `entrypointExists` check and BEFORE the idempotency pre-check (`listArgs`/`repoPath` branch) and the `add` call that actually produce the 'registered'/'unchanged'/'failed' MCP outcome — i.e. before, not after, the outcome is known. [files: src/daemon/mcp-register.ts]
findings.action: Correct the sequencing description in section 4 to 'before the MCP registration outcome is determined' so a reader relying on the contract table for ordering isn't misled.

findings.premise: VIBE_HOME is honored consistently for both the read and write defaults of the new AGENTS.md seams (invariant [[c1]]).
findings.evidence: `defaultVibeHome()` (mcp-register.ts:115-117) resolves `process.env['VIBE_HOME'] ?? join(homedir(), '.vibe')`; `upsertVibeAgentsSteering`'s default read path (`defaultVibeAgentsMdText(home())`, line 203) and default write path (`writeFileSync(join(home(), 'AGENTS.md'), ...)`, line 204) both call the same `home` function, so a read and a write in the same invocation always target the same directory.

findings.premise: The Story reuses the existing marker constants/upsert logic owned by the prior steering-inject Story without redesigning that shared contract.
findings.evidence: git status shows only src/daemon/mcp-register.ts and its test modified for this change; src/daemon/steering-inject.ts (owner of STEERING_MARKER_START/END and upsertMarkedSection) is untouched, and mcp-register.ts imports `readSteeringBlock`/`upsertMarkedSection` from it unchanged (line 35) rather than forking or altering that module.

findings.premise: The error-cases table states that when AGENTS.md is absent, the response is to 'create file with heading + marked block', and the edge-case table states an empty file yields 'heading + block written'.
findings.evidence:
`upsertMarkedSection(null, block)` in steering-inject.ts:119-125 (the function this Story reuses unmodified) returns `content: section + '
'` — only the marked span, with no heading of any kind. The Story's own test confirms this: 'upsertVibeAgentsSteering: creates AGENTS.md ... ' (mcp-register.test.ts:141-155) asserts the written text matches `/<!-- insrc:steering:start -->
STEERING BLOCK v1
<!-- insrc:steering:end -->/` with no heading text at all. [files: src/daemon/steering-inject.ts, src/daemon/__tests__/mcp-register.test.ts]
findings.action: Remove the 'heading +' wording from the error-case and edge-case rows (or state explicitly that no heading is written) so the error-path table matches the reused upsert function's real behavior.

findings.premise: Each of the four stated acceptance criteria has a proving test present in the Story's test file, and those tests assert behavior consistent with the real (not the mis-described) implementation.
findings.evidence: mcp-register.test.ts contains the create/idempotent test (ac4), the replace-preserves-surrounding-content/asset-change test (ac1/ac2/ac3), plus a malformed-marker guard test and a registerMcpClients-integration test — all pass against the actual `upsertVibeAgentsSteering`/`upsertMarkedSection` behavior (no heading, replace-in-place, VIBE_HOME-seamed).
findings.action: none — test coverage itself is sound even though two prose sections (2.2 and the error-case heading claim) are inaccurate.

summary.prose: When vibe is registered as an insrc MCP client, the daemon also ensures the user-level ~/.vibe/AGENTS.md carries the insrc steering block between the shared insrc:steering markers (the same markers and prompts/steering-block.md asset repo.add writes into repo AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, via steering-inject.ts's upsertMarkedSection). Re-registration replaces only the marked span: idempotent, and future releases change the block content by shipping a new asset. The repo AGENTS.md insrc:steering block remains the project-level source of truth.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: mcp-register.ts registers the insrc MCP per CLI; vibe has no `mcp list`, so it is pre-checked via config.toml and registered into the repo's .vibe/config.toml (upsertVibeProjectServer) or the user-global config. Nothing wrote ~/.vibe/AGENTS.md, so the insrc:steering-following rule was lost on fresh machines and could not evolve across releases.
